feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It reads polished and modern, but it is slightly repetitive and could be tightened to sharpen impact and reduce overlap across skills, projects, and experience.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete platforms/tools: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” GA4, BigQuery, Drupal, etc.  
- Writing is generally clean, professional, and credible, with a strong match between headline, competencies, and work history.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Recent Projects” repeat similar themes. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially for the freelance role and earlier positions (e.g., growth, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, cost savings).  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” mixed punctuation in bullets, and “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma. No major misspellings or typos found; grammar is strong overall.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it is slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with sharper positioning and 1–2 concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce list-like structure; replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Emphasize current positioning: enterprise web modernization, digital governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery for public-sector/member organizations.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector and membership organizations. Combines platform strategy, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search to improve how complex, mission-driven organizations communicate at scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with recent projects and core competencies; “AI-enabled search” is more specific.
- The subtitle already signals leadership, so avoid repeating too many broad capability labels here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize strategic strengths rather than repeating detailed capability areas already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reduce overlap and sharpen phrasing: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and performance insights • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “systems,” “operations,” and “experiences” inconsistently.
- Consider replacing “website” with “web” for a more senior, enterprise-level tone.
- If space is tight, cut “public-sector” or “livestream” here since those are reinforced elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats the header and Recent Projects almost verbatim.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “workflow automation and platform integration” are already covered in Topline Skills and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a repeat of the experience section and is slightly too dense for a footer. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinguishing details will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [project] to [purpose/outcome].”
- Tighten wording: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for future campaign expansion”; “bill-level AI chat” to “bill-level AI assistant” if that’s the user-facing term.
- Consider this cleaner version: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search—Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat to improve policy discovery. We Are Counties Microsite—Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and reusable modules for future expansion. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Created a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Launched a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs slightly if space allows.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with NACo themes. Tighten it around outcomes, scope, and what is new at this senior level—especially AI search, enterprise workflows, and platform improvement.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, and cross-channel content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs with impact framing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Combine overlapping web bullets into one sharper line: “Built Drupal-based campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, member toolkits, and front-end/CMS enhancements for high-traffic public sites.”
- Add measurable outcomes if possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing time reduced, search success rate, engagement lift, or stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, and cross-channel coordination” repeats NACo; keep only if you can show a new scale, method, or result.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a business outcome.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation wins, and add outcome language beyond platform size.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate and sharpen bullets around outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable business impact where possible: email engagement growth, social growth, production cost/time savings from the studio, reporting efficiency, or governance improvements.
- Tighten phrasing for parallel structure: start bullets with strong verbs like “Directed,” “Launched,” “Built,” “Expanded,” “Standardized.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; emphasize leadership scale, transformation, and systems ownership here instead of routine channel management.
- Video/studio work may echo earlier NACo multimedia bullets; frame this as building institutional capacity, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned before stepping into broader strategy, governance, and platform leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and advocacy video, coordinating editorial execution across communications, policy, and program teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy and member communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with ownership language where accurate: “Standardized editorial planning and digital publishing workflows to improve coordination, consistency, and turnaround time.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved digital publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- Weekly video/livestream language may also duplicate the prior Digital Media Manager entry; keep this version focused on scaling and operational ownership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent leadership scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with tighter, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Editorial operations & content systems
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and outcome-oriented.
- If space allows, add one impact cue in the heading or nearby summary, e.g., “for 10,000+ page platforms and multi-team publishing environments.”
- Keep terminology consistent with recent roles: use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” if that phrasing appears elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of platforms and execution skills, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal first and de-emphasize older/lower-signal platforms unless central to target roles.
- Replace “Power Pages” and possibly “SharePoint” with stronger, broader language like “enterprise web platforms” if those tools are not recent differentiators.
- Use parallel phrasing and trim filler; “AI-enabled search experiences” → “AI-enabled search and content discovery” is clearer and more outcome-oriented.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, especially because it aligns with the 2022–2024 director role. But it reads as a generic inventory; tightening the phrasing and emphasizing business use will make it feel more senior and less repetitive with Core Competencies and work bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not just tools: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery”
- Replace generic terms with outcome-oriented phrasing: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting”
- Consider a tighter version: “Analytics stack: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding • SEO and web performance analysis”
- If you have metrics, reflect them elsewhere in recent roles rather than here, e.g., reporting adoption, decision speed, or traffic/conversion improvements

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing here
- This item overlaps with the NACo bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure; keep this section tool/capability-focused, not achievement-focused

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with the broader “Multimedia & live event production” competency and several NACo experience bullets. Make it more specific to delivery capabilities and tools, not general production language.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia, Studio & Live Event Production
- Tighten and sharpen the list to: Video production & post-production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Hybrid, virtual and broadcast-style event production
- If accurate, add scale/tool specificity for credibility: e.g., multi-camera production, live switching, webinar platforms, recording workflows
- Keep wording operational and current-facing; avoid broad phrases like “event delivery” if “production” already covers it

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” overlaps with older NACo bullets; “post-production” is a cleaner, less repetitive phrasing
- This section partially duplicates Core Competencies’ “Multimedia & live event production”; make this version more technical/tactical to differentiate it

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” This item should either be tighter and more platform-specific or add light proficiency/context.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web Platforms & CMS Administration
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise content architecture, microsites, publishing workflows) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, order by relevance/recency: Drupal • SharePoint • Power Pages • WordPress • GitHub Pages
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful recent project; it feels lighter than the other platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” is already repeated in Topline Skills; avoid listing the same tools twice without added context.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so this item should emphasize platforms or level of use, not restate the category.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools tied to recent work and grouping older/front-end basics more tightly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (incl. jQuery) • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions / CI workflows
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV is similarly specific; they date the section without adding value.
- Put the strongest, more current tools first: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, API integrations, then core front-end languages.
- If accurate, add one higher-impact qualifier such as “serverless scripting,” “deployment automation,” or “tag implementation” to show application, not just exposure.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” “Workflow automation”).
- Avoid repeating the same stack in both sections; use one for broad themes and this one for specific tools only.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow architecture capability. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to a capability-led line: “Workflow automation & collaboration systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project and team operations in Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the highest-value automation tools first and group lower-value collaboration apps together to show hierarchy.
- If accurate, add scope or use case in brief: “used for editorial planning, approvals, intake, and cross-team coordination.”
- Consider trimming to the most relevant 5–7 tools, especially those tied to recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools and may add little unless they supported a notable workflow system.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the strength of the recent experience. It should signal level of use and avoid reading like an undifferentiated software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize function and scale: “Email Marketing, Journeys & Member Engagement Platforms” or “Email, Marketing Automation & Community Platforms.”
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp.”
- If accurate, add proficiency/context rather than just names, e.g. “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member email/community communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter production).”
- Keep it concise and platform-only; save outcomes for work experience bullets where email audience scale is already established.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email leadership and newsletter scale already appear in NACo roles, so don’t repeat audience-size claims here.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel language elsewhere; use platform-specific wording to keep this item distinct.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analysis/optimization capabilities rather than repeating platform names already evidenced in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics, Reporting & Optimization
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation/A/B testing
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards” to sound more outcome-oriented.
- If accurate, consider adding one stronger capability over a generic term, e.g. “data visualization,” “funnel analysis,” or “conversion analysis.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider keeping the fuller version in one place and shortening this item to tools only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 Director role, so avoid overloading this section with repeated wording.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this role more foundational/tactical, with concrete outputs and any scale metrics you can add.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and execution: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add specific outputs and scope: include number of livestreams/videos produced, frequency of weekly updates, audience growth, email volume, or website-refresh contribution.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize cross-channel publishing workflows.”
- Clarify supervision only if meaningful: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or remove if informal.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” repeat points already covered in the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching the team and hands-on production.
- Avoid broad claims about digital strategy here; reserve leadership/governance language for the more senior NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and content work at NACo. It should be tightened and framed as a foundation role, with more emphasis on the podcast launch since that is the clearest, most distinctive outcome.

Suggested edit
- Recast to emphasize progression and ownership: “Supported innovation and research initiatives for NACo programs and policy teams while contributing to early digital and multimedia communications efforts.”
- Make the podcast the lead accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “supporting organizational programs and policy work” and “contributed to digital content production”; replace with specific outputs if known.
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of multimedia assets produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Since later entries already show video/digital leadership, keep this item focused on research support + first podcast launch.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should stay tool-focused and concise.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Multimedia Tools
